evals.name: small-clear-build
evals.prompt: Build a Python CLI that sums the amount column in a CSV. Print the total; reject malformed amounts with a clear error. Standard library only.
evals.expected_output: A runnable standard-library CLI, checked against both fixtures, with no planning scaffolding.
expectations: Produces a runnable CLI and runs it on valid.csv, reporting the total 35.00 (or an equivalent representation)
Runs it on malformed.csv and shows a clear error for the malformed amount instead of a partial total
Uses only the Python standard library
Reports which checks ran and their results

evals.name: vague-scope
evals.prompt: Create a project to help my team handle incoming requests.
evals.expected_output: A focused question about the desired workflow or outcome with a recommendation, not a guessed product or a stack questionnaire.
expectations: Asks at most three questions, focused on the workflow, users, or outcome rather than the technology stack
Offers a recommended default or a concrete starting proposal the user can correct
Does not build a complete product based on guesses about what 'requests' means

evals.name: planning-endpoint
evals.prompt: Plan a local photo organizer. No implementation or generated project files yet.
evals.expected_output: A useful scoped plan in the response; no files.
expectations: Delivers a plan with scope, non-goals, acceptance checks, and a first end-to-end slice
States technical assumptions instead of requiring the user to pick a stack
Creates no code, scaffold, or project files

evals.name: resume-existing-work
evals.prompt: Resume the project and implement the next slice.
evals.expected_output: Reads recorded state, verifies it, implements and tests R2 using the existing requirements file.
expectations: Runs the recorded test command before changing code
Implements --top N with frequency order and alphabetical ties as specified in docs/requirements.md
Adds or updates a test for R2 and runs it
Updates the state of R2 in docs/requirements.md and the next action in PROJECT.md
Leaves the personal notes in notes/ideas.md untouched

evals.name: research-uncertainty
evals.prompt: Investigate whether this local dataset supports detecting topic changes over time. Research only.
evals.expected_output: A method, a baseline, a small reproducible analysis, and stated limitations, with no product build.
expectations: Defines a method and a baseline before reporting a result
Runs a small reproducible analysis on data/posts.csv, or explains why it could not
Reports the March sampling gap and near-duplicate posts as limitations
Ends with findings and a recommended next step rather than an application

evals.name: risk-in-small-tool
evals.prompt: Build a local duplicate-file finder. Report duplicates; do not remove anything. Try it on ./files.
evals.expected_output: A verified finder that reports a.txt and nested/b.txt as duplicates and leaves every file intact.
expectations: Reports files/a.txt and files/nested/b.txt as duplicates and files/c.txt as unique
Compares content, not only names or sizes
Offers no deletion feature and calls no cloud service

evals.name: missing-integrations
evals.prompt: Build a local-first task CLI: add, list, and complete tasks, stored in a local file.
evals.host_conditions: Run without specialist skills, MCP servers, an issue tracker, or subagents.
evals.expected_output: A working CLI built sequentially with the available tools.
expectations: Completes add, list, and complete with persistence across runs, and demonstrates it
Proceeds without installing a skill catalog, tracker, or other assumed integration
Reports the checks that ran

evals.name: missing-authorization
evals.prompt: Build a static portfolio page for a data analyst named Alex. Keep it local; do not publish it.
evals.expected_output: A local static site that was viewed or validated, with no publication.
expectations: Produces the page and checks it renders, for example by opening or validating it
Does not create a remote repository, push, deploy, or send messages
Explains how to view it locally

evals.name: conflicting-memory
evals.prompt: Continue the habit tracker with SQLite as we discussed just now; set up storage and the first command.
evals.expected_output: Uses SQLite, updates the stale storage decision with its reason, and keeps the rest of the record.
expectations: Uses SQLite rather than PostgreSQL
Notes the conflict with the recorded PostgreSQL decision and updates or supersedes it
Preserves the outcome and other unrelated content in PROJECT.md
Runs the first command end to end against the database

evals.name: missing-credentials
evals.prompt: Build a weather CLI using the provider described in api/contract.json. Print the current temperature for a city.
evals.host_conditions: No WEATHER_API_KEY and no network access to the provider.
evals.expected_output: Local behavior tested against fixtures; live authentication clearly reported as unverified.
expectations: Reads the key from WEATHER_API_KEY and handles the 401, 404, and 429 errors
Tests the response handling with clearly labeled fixtures or stubs
States that real authentication and the live provider call remain unverified
Does not claim or fabricate a successful live run

evals.name: scope-steering
turns: Build a small report generator that turns a CSV of sales into a summary report, as CSV and PDF.
Keep CSV output, but remove PDF support from scope.
evals.expected_output: The report objective survives; PDF leaves scope; CSV is finished and verified.
expectations: Keeps the original report objective after the correction
Removes PDF from requirements, code paths, and dependencies that were added for it
Finishes and verifies the CSV report

evals.name: discovery-boundary
evals.prompt: Fix the off-by-one bug in src/pager.py; tests/test_pager.py reproduces it.
evals.expected_output: An ordinary bug fix without project discovery.
expectations: Fixes the start offset so page 1 begins at the first item, and runs the test
Does not start project discovery or create project records

evals.name: multi-session-greenfield
evals.prompt: I want to build a self-hosted recipe manager for my family. We'll work on it over several sessions, so set it up properly and get the first useful piece working today.
evals.expected_output: A durable PROJECT.md with acceptance and state, and one end-to-end behavior working before breadth.
expectations: Asks only questions that change scope, privacy, or cost, each with a recommendation, and proceeds on the rest
Creates PROJECT.md with outcome, acceptance checks, state, and a concrete next action
Gets one end-to-end behavior (for example, add and view a recipe with persistence) running before building breadth
Avoids empty placeholder folders and speculative infrastructure

evals.name: prototype-endpoint
evals.prompt: Quick prototype: would fuzzy search over my notes folder actually be useful? Throwaway code is fine; I just want to know.
evals.expected_output: A bounded, labeled prototype run on the notes, with a finding and a recommendation.
expectations: States the question the prototype answers and how usefulness will be judged
Runs the prototype on the notes and shows representative results
Labels the code as a prototype and reports the finding with a recommended next step
Does not harden the prototype into a production project
